title: How to Get a First-Time Job Seeker Certificate (RA 11261)
description: Avail of free government documents and clearances for your first employment under the First-Time Jobseekers Assistance Act.

requirements.title: Valid ID
requirements.description: Any government-issued ID or school ID for recent graduates.

requirements.title: Proof of Residency
requirements.description: Documents proving you have lived in the barangay for at least 6 months.

requirements.title: Oath of Undertaking
requirements.description: A signed document provided by the barangay hall.

checklist.title: Prepare IDs
checklist.description: Gather your valid ID or proof of education before visiting the barangay hall.

checklist.title: Visit Barangay Hall
checklist.description: Go to the administrative office of the barangay where you reside.

checklist.title: Sign Oath
checklist.description: Request and sign the Oath of Undertaking affirming your status as a first-time job seeker.

checklist.title: Receive Certificate
checklist.description: Claim your signed certificate, which is issued free of charge and valid for one year.

content.title: What is the First-Time Job Seeker Certificate?

blocks.content: The **First-Time Job Seeker Certificate** is a document issued by your local Barangay under **Republic Act No. 11261** (First-Time Jobseekers Assistance Act).
It allows qualified Filipinos who are looking for their first job to get various government-issued documents and clearances **free of charge**.

The certificate is commonly used to waive fees for:
*   NBI Clearance
*   Police Clearance (National)
*   PSA Birth and Marriage Certificates
*   Barangay Clearance (for employment)
*   Medical Certificate from public hospitals
*   Tax Identification Number (TIN) application

You may need a First-Time Job Seeker Certificate if you are:
- A fresh graduate (College, High School, or Vocational)
- An out-of-school youth (OSY)
- A student on leave of absence seeking work
- Any Filipino citizen who has never been employed (formal or informal)

content.title: Benefits of Having a First-Time Job Seeker Certificate

blocks.content: Obtaining this certificate significantly reduces the financial burden of pre-employment requirements.

blocks.title: Fee Waivers
blocks.content: You can save between ₱500 to ₱2,000 in total by waiving the processing fees of multiple government agencies.

blocks.title: Ease of Application
blocks.content: Most agencies (like NBI and PNP) have integrated "First-Time Job Seeker" options into their online portals, making the process smoother.

blocks.title: Walk-In Application
blocks.content: This is the only method available, as you must sign the **Oath of Undertaking** in person before a barangay official.
**Pro Tip:** Check if your LGU has an **Online Portal**. Many cities now allow you to pay for Cedula or Police Clearance via GCash and just pick it up.

blocks.title: Visit your Barangay Hall
blocks.content: Go to the administrative office of the Barangay where you have resided for at least 6 months.

blocks.title: Request the Forms
blocks.content: Ask the staff for the **First-Time Job Seeker Certification** and the **Oath of Undertaking** form.

blocks.title: Fill Out and Sign
blocks.content: Fill out your personal details and sign the **Oath of Undertaking**. By signing this, you swear that you are a first-time job seeker and have not yet availed of these benefits.

blocks.title: Claim Your Certificate
blocks.content: The Barangay Chairman or an authorized official will sign your certificate. It is issued **free of charge** and is usually ready within minutes.

Applicants may process their First-Time Job Seeker Certificate at:
- Your local Barangay Hall (Barangay Office)

Typical processing timelines include:
*   Walk-in: 15–30 Minutes (Same Day)
Since the document is issued immediately, there is no online tracking system. You receive the physical copy right after signing.

Applicants may experience:
- **Residency Issues:** If you recently moved, you may not meet the 6-month requirement.
- **Lost Certificate:** You can only avail of the free documents once. If you lose the certificate, you may have to pay for your clearances normally.

items: **Using it twice:** The law only allows you to avail of the free services **once**.
**Expired Certificate:** The certificate is only valid for **one (1) year**. Use it to get all your clearances before it expires.

blocks.content: Always review the information on the certificate for typos before leaving the Barangay Hall.

items: Bring your own black pen to sign the forms.
Have photocopies of your ID and diploma ready just in case.
Go during mid-morning (9 AM to 11 AM) when the office is less crowded.

blocks.content:
For the most accurate and up-to-date information, please refer to:
*   Your local **Barangay Hall website** or visit the **Barangay Office** directly.
*   [Republic Act No. 11261 (First-Time Jobseekers Assistance Act)](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/2019/04/10/republic-act-no-11261/)

blocks.title: Is there an age limit?
blocks.content: No, as long as you are a first-time job seeker, you can avail of the benefits regardless of age.

blocks.title: Can I get a free Passport with this?
blocks.content: No, the Passport fee is **not** included in the list of waived fees under RA 11261.
